issue_context.title: [KEP-4639] Specify SELinux behavior for image volumes
issue_context.body:
Related to https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/47588 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126806

SIG storage meeting notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-8KEG8AjAgKznS9NFm3qWqkGyCHmvU6HVl0sk5hwoAE/edit#heading=h.9rsna5zrjwc

From me:

https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/47588#discussion_r1727171579 It is related to image volume plugin and selinux. Is it a known limitation of all the volume plugins when using selinux? I have a different opinion. If two pods don't share the same mountpoint (hostpath), they can run the same node when the selinux is enabled. the current implementation of  cri-o is sharing the same hostpath when two pods use the same image volume. More details about my idea: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126806#discussion_r1724826814 

From @jsafrane:

Sharing each volume between namespaces is kind of natural. Sharing PVs not possible but sharing image quite common.

From @gnufied: 

Although for most volume plugins it is true that, they can't be mounted with 2 different selinux context on same node, we want to understand why is this not possible for Imagevolume source. For a traditional storage persistent storage plugins - this limitation is underlying limitation of storage backend/Linux kernel etc.

For ImageVolume source, it seems like a simple solution which unpacks image to two different hostpath would work and not run into this limitation. @haircommander can you specify, why this limitation exists for ImageVolume plugins?

From @haircommander:

we choose to keep it simple and follow the lead of other volume types. supporting multiple selinux types would mean making more complicated the way we mount the image into the container AFAIR. But agreed we can chat about this elsewhere, in the meantime for the purposes of this PR: this is consistent with behavior of other volume plugins and is expected behavior.

Let's discuss the SELinux behavior for image volumes in this issue.

cc @gnufied @jsafrane @saschagrunert @haircommander

/sig node
/sig storage
comments: In my opinion, from an end-user perspective, the image volume may act like a read-only `emptydir` with a pre-populated content via image. Two pods from different namespaces can share the same image and run on the same node.

Pasted from https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/47588
> this is an intentional decision we made as it matches current volume behavior (it was discussed offline in a convo with @gnufied so I can't link unfortunately). I agree with known limitation, or maybe even design decision that some users need to react to. it's not unique to cri-o, it's just that cri-o often runs on nodes that run SELinux

According to @wzshiming's [comment](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/10579#issuecomment-2309595333), the containerd doesn't have the same limitation.

Given that OCI/Image Volume Source support is in alpha, I'd prefer that we consider discussing this as part of the original feature. We can discuss this here but I don't know if we need a separate KEP for this yet.

> According to @wzshiming's https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/10579#issuecomment-2309595333, the containerd doesn't have the same limitation.

Yes, so far, in our conversations at the containerd community meetings we decided to start this feature out using a single pod scope for the pod scoped image volume host path because in containerd each runtime handler may have a different snapshotter (possibly on a different fs), or at least that's the plan. Additionally, the pods may have different os versions on windows indicating a different platform can be selected on the same node and this sort of versioning may extend beyond to other os providers. We could ask Kirtana to confirm the versioning issue and status of platform version selection over the platform index manifest, if the snapshotter reason isn't enough to at least start with per pod scope.  

If this is insufficient support we can certainly discuss.  

Cheers, Mike

>  but I don't know if we need a separate KEP for this yet.

No need a separate KEP. We can update the original KEP once this issue is resolved.
I'm working on a technical solution (just a PoC) in https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/pull/8521, not sure how feasible that is as time of writing, though.

yeah I agree I don't think we need a different feature for this, especially because it's mostly an implementation detail in the runtime. @carlory would you open this as an issue in kubernetes/kubernetes instead of the enhancements repo, or even better in the cri-o repo?
@haircommander I moved this issue into kubernetes repo.

Copid from kep:

```
SELinux
Traditionally, the container runtime is responsible of applying SELinux labels to volume mounts, which are inherited from the securityContext of the pod or container on container creation. The same will apply to OCI volume mounts.
```

As https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/pull/8521 merged, do we need to change the KEPs to reflect the new behavior? @saschagrunert
@carlory no, nothing needs to be changed from a Kubernetes any more :+1:
